run.market_summary: 1) The Fed has turned hawkish. It raised rates for the first time since 2023, and Waller is now openly floating a 50bp hike in December. A strong October jobs report (+165k, unemployment 4.1%) backs him up. This is the main signal, but the market isn't fully buying it yet: SPY, QQQ and IWM are flat to up over 5 days, the dollar (UUP) hasn't moved, and long bonds (TLT) are slightly up. 2) Nvidia's 'Huang scandal' is pushing Congress toward a full ban on AI chip exports to China, and Republicans are now joining in. NVDA has already fallen 11.6% to its most oversold level since 2019, while AMD has rallied 8.9% even though it faces the same China export risk. 3) Iran de-escalation has pushed Brent below $90. USO, XLE and JETS have each moved 8-9% in a week, so that trade is mostly done. Overall: three of the four headline themes are already in prices. The cleanest gap left is the hawkish Fed against flat rate-sensitive assets. Keep total exposure to the hawkish-Fed idea small, because UUP and TLT are related bets.

ideas.thesis: The Fed has made its first hike since 2023, and Waller is putting a 50bp December move on the table. Yet the dollar is flat over 5 days, so the widening rate gap hasn't been priced. Falling oil also eases a source of pressure on the dollar's terms of trade without hurting the US rate advantage.

Waller's 'half-point in the mix' and 'inflation could warrant larger increase' comments are a direct hawkish shock, but TLT is actually up 0.3% on the week. That leaves room for long yields to reprice ahead of the December meeting.

AMD rose 8.9% as traders rotated out of NVDA after the scandal. But the bill Congress is pushing would block all AI chip exports to China, which hits AMD's China accelerator sales too. The rally ignores that shared risk, and the hawkish Fed adds pressure on high-valuation semis.

analysis.headline: Hotter-than-expected October CPI (headline +0.4%, core +0.3%, which meets Waller's stated bar for considering a 50bp hike) sent the 10-year yield back to about 5% (+12bp) and lifted the dollar while gold and TIPS fell. Stocks gapped lower but recovered most of the gap during the session. The day's real equity damage was concentrated in Nvidia (−5.5% on 3x volume, Huang scandal) and Microsoft (−2.2%, Anthropic Office-style tools).
analysis.narrative:
This was a rates day, not an equity day. The 1.5σ+ moves were almost all in rates and FX: 10-year +12bp to 4.98% (z +2.0), TLT −1.3% (z −1.9), UUP +0.6% (z +1.9), TIP −0.7% (z −2.8, the largest z on the board), GLD −2.7% (z −1.6). The setup started overnight with Waller (04:00 ET) leaning toward a December hike and saying a half-point move should be considered if core CPI came in around 0.3%. The 08:30 print gave him exactly that: headline +0.4% against +0.3% expected, and core +0.3%, a tenth above consensus. Yields gapped only +4bp but added another +8bp during the session, and the 10-year crossed 5% in the afternoon. That was helped by Dallas Fed's Logan saying two more hikes would be needed. TIPS fell even though the 1-year inflation swap dropped below 2% on cheaper oil and gasoline, so this was a real-yield and policy shock, not a breakeven scare. That explains gold falling with crypto (BTC −1.8%, COIN/MSTR/HOOD −2.4% to −3.6%).

Equities took the hawkish repricing surprisingly calmly. Every index and sector ETF moved less than 1σ. SPY gapped −0.63% and then gained +0.26% during the session, even as yields kept rising. VIX fell 2.3%, and breadth split 6 of 13 sectors up. Defensive and value areas (XLF +0.5%, XLV, XLP, XLC) held up. Energy (gap −1.7%, intraday +2.2%), industrials and materials bought the dip. The equity weakness was concentrated in tech: XLK −1.15%, QQQ −0.68%. Two single-stock stories account for most of it. NVDA fell 5.5% on 3.1x volume as the Jensen Huang/alleged-Chinese-spy story widened, with the board hiring outside counsel, Republicans threatening a subpoena, and Congress pushing a full AI-chip export ban. MSFT fell 2.2%, almost all of it during the session, after Anthropic announced workplace tools that compete with Office, a few days before its ~$1T+ IPO.

The rest of semis did not trade like an industry-wide export-control shock. SMH recovered +1.1% after the open, AMD lost only 1.3%, and AVGO rose 3.9% during the session, extending Monday's +8.8%. That fits money moving out of NVDA into custom-silicon and peer names more than a sector-wide de-rating. Single-name stories: NKE −3% (Investor Day pushed the recovery out; BofA cut estimates and now sees recovery in 2028), NUE +2.9% (Q3 profit doubled and the Q4 outlook held), OXY +2.0% (Q3 beat, plus the energy-sector rebound during the session).

analysis.cross_asset_read: Textbook hawkish-policy shock in rates and FX: yields up, dollar up, gold down, TIPS down, crypto down. Falling breakevens (1-year swap below 2%) mean it was real yields doing the work, which explains gold and BTC falling together. Equities did not confirm risk-off. VIX fell, SPY rose during the session as the 10-year crossed 5%, and losses were concentrated in two stocks with their own news (NVDA, MSFT). Value and financials beat growth. Oil was flat, so energy's +2.2% after the open was a rotation or bounce, not crude-driven. The rate-stock disconnect in equities is the thing to watch: with 5% on the 10-year and a likely 50bp debate, equities may be underpricing duration risk, or else the market sees the hikes as credible inflation control.

model_grade.summary: Strong day for the morning model. Its main call, a hawkish Fed under-priced in rates and FX, played out almost perfectly, and all three trade ideas made money. It underweighted inflation as a separate driver even though CPI came out 25 minutes after the run, and it overstated chip export controls as a sector theme when the damage was mostly NVDA-specific.
got_right: monetary_policy +0.74 was the dominant driver: 10-year +12bp, UUP +0.62% (z +1.9), TLT −1.32% (z −1.9)
SHORT AMD: −1.30% (−1.67% vs SPY), as chip pressure persisted
Called the oil/Iran trade 'mostly done': crude only −0.46%, and XLE rebounded during the session
got_wrong: inflation scored only +0.17 although CPI was the day's catalyst; it should have been scored well above that given Waller's explicit CPI-dependent 50bp threshold
chip_export_controls +0.44 implies a broad semis hit, but SMH was only −0.8% with a strong recovery after the open and AVGO +3.9%; the move was NVDA/Huang governance risk
Said SPY/QQQ were flat to up over 5 days; they were actually −0.6% and −1.5%
missed: Gold/GLD −2.7% and TIP −0.7% (z −2.8), the cleanest expressions of the real-yield shock
Anthropic product launch hitting MSFT (−2.2%) and the AI-disruption theme ahead of the Anthropic IPO
Equities shrugging off rising yields after the open (cyclicals and energy bid)
NKE Investor Day downgrade; defense names rallying despite de-escalation

lessons: When a Fed speaker sets an explicit data threshold (e.g. 'core 0.3% → consider 50bp') and the print comes out the same morning, raise the inflation score in line with that threshold. Don't run it at +0.17 while monetary_policy sits at +0.74.
Add short GLD / short TIP as companion expressions to hawkish-Fed ideas when breakevens are falling (oil down): the real-yield shock showed up most cleanly there (TIP z −2.8).

Separate company-specific governance risk from sector-wide export-control risk. Hedge an NVDA-specific scandal against peers rather than shorting the sector (AVGO +3.9%, SMH recovered during the session).
Track pending AI-lab product launches and IPOs (Anthropic) as a disruption risk for incumbent software (MSFT).
Don't assume rate shocks pass through to equity indexes. Today a z +2 yield move produced only z −0.3 in SPY, so size equity shorts off rates ideas cautiously.
